analyzed_vuln.description: constantPropagate dereferences `this->variable()->initialValue()` and may clone it without verifying that the `Variable` still points to a live declaration/value node. During CFG optimization/rescans, IR nodes in the pool can be replaced/poisoned while stale `VariableReference`/`Variable::fDeclaration` links remain, so `Variable::initialValue()` returns a pointer into poisoned memory (`fDeclaration->value().get()`), causing the use-after-poison read seen in `unique_ptr::get`. The root bug is unsafe propagation using stale variable-declaration state, not the accessor itself.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered by compiling/optimizing crafted SkSL that causes optimizer rewrites/rescans (via `Compiler::scanCFG` -> `simplifyExpression` -> `VariableReference::constantPropagate`) while a read-reference to a const/local variable survives after its declaration/value storage has been invalidated/replaced. In the provided PoC (`void a(){if(2>2)int a;a;}`), optimization of unreachable/undefined-flow code leads to stale definition/declaration pointers; then constant propagation reads `variable()->initialValue()` and accesses poisoned pool memory.
